safety_arguments.argument: Safe sequential Rust with explicit owned inputs. The workspace unsafe_code forbid lint is the owned-unsafe basis, and no compiler foreign-item fact exists for this crate; absent function-safety facts are not unsafe evidence.

Safe no_std frontend with explicit owned source bytes and an inward dependency on noble-kernel. The workspace unsafe_code forbid lint is the owned-unsafe basis; native accounting must confirm the absence of foreign-item facts.

Safe no_std emitter with explicit owned checked-kernel and checked WIT export inputs and allocation limits, depending inward on noble-kernel and noble-contracts. The workspace unsafe_code forbid lint is the owned-unsafe basis; native accounting must confirm the absence of foreign-item facts. Emitting or byte-binding owned WAT does not prove those fragments, backend lowering, loader binding or Wasm execution semantics. The selected Miri subject remains the kernel budget test and does not establish emitter execution coverage.

Composition-root orchestration invokes external JSON/Wasm parsers, Wasmtime execution, digest generation and Linux filesystem flags. The workspace forbids owned unsafe_code in this crate, but does not audit external unsafe implementations, engine behavior, host resource lifetime or command authority; those require the caller checks and explicit assumptions above.

Safe std composition-root policy serializes bounded M7 table access with a Mutex and host-owned AtomicU64 session identity. The workspace unsafe_code forbid lint is the owned-unsafe basis; compiler accounting must confirm no foreign-item facts and no third-party production dependencies. Host-assigned facets and engine trap authenticity remain explicit assumptions; source inventory leaves new choreography/parser/refinement bodies open.

scope_note: Five-crate workspace scope: noble-kernel, noble-contracts, noble-wasm, noble-cli and noble-syndicate on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu. This records native Rust and dependency scope, not whole-program soundness or Wasm runtime correspondence. Owned WAT assets and Node/wasm-tools/Binaryen subprocesses are separately byte-bound by tool selection; their semantics are unproved and are not Rust inventory subjects or native linked dependencies. The independent Wasmtime verification peers are separate Cargo workspaces, with the M8 peer's external Cargo lock derived exactly from the reviewed M7 peer lock and selected source/vendor NAR identities. Engine behavior, native resource lifetime and host credential provenance remain explicit assumptions, not production dependency or unsafe-code discharge.

assumptions: strict provenance is the required Miri model
The compiler/Cargo inventory does not audit linked system libraries or transitive native/unsafe dependency implementations; no owned foreign-item fact is not a linker-closure or host-ABI proof
Core-Bootstrap managed-linear-memory execution, Component-Sync-Bootstrap and the two M3 Wasm experiments are separately scoped guest execution, not additional claimed native Rust targets
